findings.title: Supabase service role key committed to public git history
findings.description: Real SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY committed in May 2025, repo is public. Key bypasses all RLS.
findings.exploit_scenario: git clone repo -> git show 963fe19 | grep SERVICE_ROLE_KEY -> query Supabase REST API with full service-role access
findings.impact: Complete database access: read/write/delete all founder data, submissions, traction, reviews
findings.recommendation: Rotate key immediately in Supabase dashboard. Update Render env var. Audit Supabase logs for abuse. Clean git history with git filter-repo.

findings.title: RAG poisoning — founder submissions injected into AI system prompt
findings.description: Founder submission text is embedded into vector store and retrieved directly into the system prompt with 'Treat as primary evidence' instruction. Enables prompt injection via crafted submission content.
findings.exploit_scenario: Founder submits 'IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS...' -> embedding pipeline stores it -> buildSemanticContext retrieves it -> staff AI advisor follows injected instructions with privileged tool access
findings.impact: Exfiltration of other teams' data, attacker-controlled AI behavior with staff-level tools
findings.recommendation: Sanitize submission text before embedding. Label retrieved chunks as user-submitted content that should not be followed as instructions.

findings.title: Upload route accepts any file type — stored XSS vector
findings.description: File type (user-controlled) is passed directly to Supabase Storage as contentType. No MIME or extension allowlist. Allows uploading HTML/SVG files that browsers render as HTML.
findings.exploit_scenario: Upload xss.html with Content-Type: text/html to avatars bucket -> share public URL -> victim's session cookies stolen via script execution
findings.recommendation: Add per-bucket MIME type allowlist. Reject uploads not matching allowed types.

findings.title: /admin/auth-monitoring accessible to any logged-in user
findings.description: Page presents as admin dashboard with no role enforcement. Any authenticated user can access it.
findings.exploit_scenario: Logged-in user navigates to /admin/auth-monitoring -> sees admin dashboard UI
findings.impact: Information disclosure, unauthorized access to admin tooling surface
findings.recommendation: Delete app/admin/ directory entirely — it is a development leftover.

findings.title: TypeScript and ESLint errors silently ignored in production builds
findings.description: ignoreBuildErrors and ignoreDuringBuilds suppress type errors in prod. Security-relevant type bugs deploy without warning.
findings.exploit_scenario: Type error in auth path goes undetected -> ships to prod -> exploitable null dereference or auth bypass
findings.recommendation: Remove both flags from next.config.mjs. Fix surfacing type errors.
